title: Delete dead AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers (logger.dart:85-94) — near-duplicate of the live crashlytics_bootstrap.dart handler wiring
rule: Fowler-duplication (dead code / duplicate responsibility); EH-1 context
why: Repo-wide grep for `setupFlutterErrorHandlers` shows its only 3 call sites are all inside logger_test.dart; bootstrap.dart never calls it, calling bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers() instead. Git history proves this is not an oversight but a leftover: commit 78479109 (DNI-319/Story 24.4) deleted the `AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers();` call from main.dart and replaced it inline with the Crashlytics-forwarding block that is now crashlytics_bootstrap.dart:26-34 — but never deleted the method or its dedicated test group. Both implementations assign FlutterError.onError and PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError unconditionally (no chaining), so whichever runs last wins outright. Because the dead method is public, documented, and sits in core/logging/logger.dart right next to AppLogger — exactly where a future maintainer would look to 'wire up error logging' — a single future call to `AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers()` (e.g. added to a new bootstrap path, a test harness, or a plugin init) would silently clobber the crashlytics_bootstrap.dart handlers and permanently disable recordFlutterFatalError/recordError(fatal:true) reporting to Crashlytics for the rest of the process, with no compiler error and no currently-existing test able to catch it.
recommendation: Delete setupFlutterErrorHandlers() from logger.dart and its test group from logger_test.dart (see the paired TQ-8 finding). If a Talker-only path is still wanted for some caller, have crashlytics_bootstrap.dart's bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers() be the single call site and inline the two-line Talker forward there — do not keep two independent implementations of the same two global handler assignments.
acceptance_criteria: lib/core/logging/logger.dart no longer defines a function that assigns FlutterError.onError / PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError outside of core/logging's own internal use.

New Rule-0 grep (wired into `make audit`) asserts `FlutterError\.onError\s*=` and `PlatformDispatcher\.instance\.onError\s*=` each appear in exactly one non-test, non-generated file under lib/, failing with file:line of any extra assignment site.

title: Guard AuthStateNotifier._init() against I/O exceptions so auth state never hangs at AuthState.initializing() forever

evidence.quote:
if (firebaseUser != null) {
      final refreshed = await authRepo.reloadCurrentUser();

/// App has not yet resolved the initial session (splash window).
  /// Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.

why: build() kicks _init() fire-and-forget and returns AuthState.initializing() immediately; _init() then awaits 4+ Firebase/DAO calls (reloadCurrentUser, findCloudBornByFirebaseUid, getUserProfileByFirebaseUid, upgradeLocalToCloud, findByTier) with zero try/catch anywhere in the method. AuthState has exactly 3 statuses (initializing/signedOut/signedIn) — there is no error state — so any exception during _init() (a DB read failure, a Firebase reload throwing) is an unhandled Future rejection that leaves sessionStatus permanently stuck at `initializing`. This directly contradicts the domain model's own doc comment: 'Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.' Every screen gating on authStateProvider (router, app_shell, sign-in flows) would show a permanent splash/loading state with no retry path, recoverable only by force-killing the app. EH-1's global PlatformDispatcher.onError would log the exception, but nothing resets `state`, so the hang persists regardless of logging.
recommendation: Wrap _init()'s body in try/catch (or convert the class to a plain function-style Future<AuthState> build via AsyncNotifier<AuthState> + AsyncValue.guard); on any caught exception, log via AppLogger and fall back to `state = const AuthState.signedOut()` rather than leaving `initializing` unresolved.
acceptance_criteria: _init() cannot leave sessionStatus at initializing on any exception path — it resolves to signedIn or signedOut every time, with the failure logged via AppLogger.

Regression test: override authRepositoryProvider/userDatabaseProvider with a fake that throws from reloadCurrentUser() (and separately from the DAO) during _init(); assert authStateProvider settles to a terminal state within the test, not stuck at initializing.

Rule-0 checker: none exists yet; add a heuristic grep/custom_lint (once custom_lint is unbroken) flagging a Notifier's build() that calls an unawaited private async method with zero try/catch in that method's body.

corrections: Cited rule SM-5 governs AsyncValue<T>-typed provider state (AsyncLoading/AsyncValue.guard) and explicitly bans manual try/catch state assignment; AuthStateNotifier's state is a custom AuthState (not AsyncValue), confirmed by auth_state_provider.g.dart:28 (`$NotifierProvider<AuthStateNotifier, AuthState>`). Correct citation is SM-2 (build must be pure/no side effects — build() kicks _init() fire-and-forget). The finding's primary recommendation (manual try/catch assigning state) contradicts the very SM-5 clause it invokes; only its parenthetical AsyncNotifier+AsyncValue.guard alternative is actually SM-5-compliant.

isInitializing (auth_state.dart:75) is never read by any router guard or screen except its own domain test — confirmed by grep across app/router/**, features/**/screens/**. This contradicts the finding's 'permanent splash/loading state ... recoverable only by force-killing the app' claim. Also: rule citation SM-5 is a misfit — SM-5 governs AsyncValue<T>-based AsyncNotifier mutations ('let build throw; never hand-manage loading/error with try/catch that assigns state'), but AuthStateNotifier's state is a plain custom AuthState (not AsyncValue), and the finding's own recommendation (add try/catch, manually assign state) is the literal opposite of what SM-5 mandates. EH-2 ('raw exception must never propagate into presentation... convert to a value at the data-layer boundary') is the better-fitting rule for this defect.

The claim 'every screen gating on authStateProvider ... would show a permanent splash/loading state' is false: `AuthState.isInitializing` (auth_state.dart:75) has no callers in lib/ — no widget, guard, or splash screen branches on SessionStatus.initializing. All real consumers (app_shell.dart:140,152,453; profile_providers.dart:23,79; auth_guard.dart) read isSignedIn/isCloudBorn/currentUser, which are identical for initializing and signedOut states, so a failed _init() silently degrades to signed-out-equivalent behavior rather than hanging any UI. Recommend re-filing at P2 citing SM-2 (side-effectful build) rather than SM-5, with corrected consequence: silent session-restore failure treated as signed-out, not a permanent splash/force-kill hang.

title: Migrate SignInController's hand-rolled Idle/Submitting/Error state to AsyncNotifier + AsyncValue.guard

evidence.quote:
// DG-GAUTH-01: signInWithGoogle() returned without throwing (no
        // user-cancel / interrupt) but left currentUser null — a silent JWT

why: SignInController extends plain `Notifier<SignInState>` (a hand-written sealed union: SignInIdle/SignInSubmitting/SignInError) instead of `AsyncNotifier<void>`, then hand-manages the loading/error lifecycle with ~15 manual `state = ...` assignments spread across try/catch/finally blocks in signInWithEmail and signInWithGoogle — duplicating exactly what AsyncValue.guard provides for free. This maps cleanly onto AsyncValue<void> (AsyncLoading=Submitting, AsyncData(null)=Idle, AsyncError=Error) but the team hand-rolled it instead. The class's own DG-GAUTH-01 comment documents a previously-shipped bug caused by exactly this pattern: a code path where signInWithGoogle() completed without throwing but left currentUser null previously fell through with 'zero feedback' (state silently stayed at whatever it was rather than transitioning to Error) — proof this hand-rolled machinery has already let a state-transition gap through undetected by the type system. Any new branch added to this 1017-line method carries the same risk; AsyncValue.guard would make 'forgot to set error state' structurally much harder.
recommendation: Migrate to `class SignInController extends AsyncNotifier<void>` (or keep the SignInIdle/Submitting/Error shape but derive it FROM an underlying AsyncValue via a getter) so state transitions on the unhappy path are guaranteed by the framework rather than manually tracked across ~15 call sites.
acceptance_criteria: No code path in signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle can leave `state` at SignInSubmitting after the method's Future completes (success or failure) — verified structurally by the AsyncNotifier/AsyncValue.guard migration rather than by manual review.

Regression test: extend the existing ensureCloudEmailVerifiedForTest-style coverage with a case asserting that EVERY awaited external call, if it throws, ends in `state is SignInError`/`AsyncError` — not silently at Idle/Submitting.

Rule-0 checker: once custom_lint is unbroken, add a rule flagging hand-rolled sealed `*State` classes with Idle/Submitting/Error (or Loading/Success/Failure)-shaped variants used as Notifier state as SM-5 AsyncNotifier-migration candidates.

corrections: DG-GAUTH-01 comment (L906-910) actually describes a missed postcondition check (googleUser == null after a successful call), not a case where state 'silently stayed' un-transitioned — the prior bug explicitly returned SignInIdle; AsyncValue.guard would not have structurally prevented it since no exception was thrown. Also 'this 1017-line method' is a misnomer — the FILE is 1016 lines; the largest method (signInWithEmail) is ~186 lines. Neither error changes the core verdict: the file, and both target methods, are real, live, and match SM-5's named anti-pattern.

title: AuthStateNotifier._init() must guard reloadCurrentUser() so an offline cold start cannot hang the session state forever

evidence.quote:
if (firebaseUser != null) {
      final refreshed = await authRepo.reloadCurrentUser();

/// App has not yet resolved the initial session (splash window).
  /// Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.

why: FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl.reloadCurrentUser() calls User.reload(), a network round-trip that throws FirebaseAuthException(network-request-failed) when offline — an entirely ordinary cold-start condition for an offline-first app (this exact file set otherwise engineers carefully around it, e.g. sign_in_controller.dart wraps every Firestore/Firebase call in try/catch and timeouts). Nothing in AuthStateNotifier._init() catches this; the exception escapes the fire-and-forget call from build(), so `state` never advances past AuthState.initializing(). AuthGuard never touches Firebase and lets onboarded users straight through to the app shell, which reads authStateProvider downstream — so a returning cloud-born user opening the app with no connectivity can be stuck on an unresolved session state indefinitely, directly violating the SessionStatus.initializing doc comment's own 'must not hang' contract (a lesson the codebase already learned once for the router guard per the '19.6 startup hardening' reference, but that didn't carry over to this newer Notifier-based path).
recommendation: Wrap the Firebase-touching logic in _init() (at minimum the reloadCurrentUser() call) in try/catch; on failure, fall back to trusting the cached bare currentUser or the local-born row rather than leaving state unset, mirroring the defensive timeout/try-catch pattern already used elsewhere in sign_in_controller.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: mock AuthRepository.reloadCurrentUser() to throw (simulating an offline reload()), build AuthStateNotifier, and assert state resolves to a terminal SessionStatus within a bounded time instead of remaining initializing indefinitely.
On-device check: cold-start the app in airplane mode with a previously-active cloud-born session and confirm no indefinite splash/loading hang.

corrections: The cited rule AU-4 is misapplied. AU-4's actual text/Why ("Gate startup/session routing on authStateChanges()/idTokenChanges() streams, never a bare currentUser read... currentUser can be null before auth finishes initializing (startup race)") addresses a different defect: using authRepo.currentUser (a bare synchronous read, which _init() also does at line 31) instead of subscribing to the auth-state stream. It says nothing about catching exceptions from reload()/network calls. The defect this finding actually demonstrates — an unhandled exception escaping an unguarded async call and permanently stalling state — is better characterized as an EH-2 violation (raw exception not converted to a value at the data boundary) or filed as a standalone violation of the in-code 'must not hang' invariant, not AU-4. Severity P1 is still justified independently via the digest's 'violated named invariant' clause, and the recommendation (wrap in try/catch, fall back gracefully) is sound regardless of the rule mislabel — but the ticket's rule tag should be corrected before filing.

AuthGuard (learning_tracker/lib/app/router/guards/auth_guard.dart) never reads authStateProvider/Firebase — it only checks SharedPreferences onboarding flags and a local DeviceRegistryDatabase, so it does not gate on session state and there is no confirmed navigation/splash hang. SessionStatus.isInitializing is unused in all production code (grep confirms only its own definition and one unit test reference), so nothing currently blocks/waits on it. The actual confirmed consequence is silent downstream misbehavior in currentAccountIdProvider (falls back to profileId 1), autoSelectedProfileId (returns null), RestoreGuard.hasCloudAccount, and app_shell's offline-banner/upgrade-nudge logic — not an indefinite UI hang. Rule citation AU-4 is a loose fit; EH-2/EH-3 (uncaught exception not converted to a value at the boundary) better describes the mechanism, though the bare `authRepo.currentUser` read at line 31 is a genuine literal AU-4 violation worth folding in.

title: Add a getIdToken(forceRefresh) primitive so a synced write hitting permission-denied/unauthenticated can recover

evidence.quote:
if (user == null) return null;
    await user.reload();

/// Delegates to the auth gateways in `lib/core/auth/`. Per layering rule 3,
/// this file MUST NOT import the firebase_auth SDK

why: AU-5 requires exactly one getIdToken(true) forced refresh plus a single retry when a synced write fails with permission-denied/unauthenticated. A repo-wide grep for 'getIdToken' returns zero hits in lib/. Neither FirebaseAuthGateway/FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl nor AuthRepository/AuthRepositoryImpl — the only classes layering Rule 3 permits to touch FirebaseAuth for this feature — expose any way to force-refresh the cached ID token; the closest method, reloadCurrentUser()/User.reload(), only refreshes profile fields (displayName, emailVerified), not the JWT/claims. A stale token (e.g. after a custom-claims change) therefore has no dedicated recovery path; a failing synced write can only retry against the same stale token via the outbox's generic exponential backoff until it dead-letters, and the only user-facing fix is a full sign-out/sign-in.
recommendation: Add Future<String?> getIdToken({bool forceRefresh = false}) to FirebaseAuthGateway/AuthRepository as a thin pass-through to User.getIdToken, and wire the outbox/push-pipeline's permission-denied handler to call it once with forceRefresh: true plus a single retry before falling through to the existing backoff.
acceptance_criteria: FirebaseAuthGateway/AuthRepository gain a getIdToken(forceRefresh: true) method with a unit test against the fake/mock gateway.
Outbox/push-pipeline regression test: inject permission-denied on first attempt, assert exactly one getIdToken(true) call plus one retry occurs before falling back to normal backoff.

title: Wire AuthStateNotifier to authStateChanges() instead of leaving a shadowed, unused stream-based authStateProvider
why: auth_providers.dart defines a genuinely stream-backed authStateProvider (Stream<AppUser?> authState(ref) => ref.watch(authRepositoryProvider).onAuthStateChanged()) — exactly the AU-4-compliant primitive. But the provider that actually drives session routing everywhere (AuthGuard, AppShell, this screen) is the differently-implemented, identically-named authStateProvider generated from AuthStateNotifier, which never watches or listens to that stream — forcing every screen needing both to hide/alias one of them (see the 'hide authStateProvider' import here and the 'as auth_state' alias in sign_in_controller.dart/signup_screen.dart). If Firebase invalidates a session server-side (disabled account, revoked refresh token, forced sign-out elsewhere) while the app is running, nothing re-derives AuthStateNotifier's state from that change — the app keeps believing the user is signed in until an unrelated explicit action happens to call reload/signOut. account_picker_screen.dart:274 shows the same non-reactive pattern at tile-badge granularity: hasValidSession is a one-shot ref.read(...).currentUser snapshot, not derived from the stream.
recommendation: Either delete the dead stream-based authState/authStateProvider if genuinely unused, or have AuthStateNotifier subscribe to it in build() so live Firebase-side session changes propagate into routing state, removing the need for every consumer to route around the name collision.
acceptance_criteria: authStateProvider resolves to exactly one declaration reachable without hide/as workarounds across the codebase.
